column1: employer|A person or organisation that pays people to work.|Your employer must receive the completed tax form.
employee|Someone paid to work for an organisation.|Each employee receives a security pass.
staff|The people employed by an organisation.|All staff must attend the safety briefing.
colleague|Someone you work with.|Ask a colleague to show you the filing system.
manager|Someone responsible for a team or business.|Please discuss your holiday request with the manager.
supervisor|Someone who oversees other people's work.|Your supervisor will check the completed order.
team|A group of people working towards a shared goal.|Our team handles customer enquiries.
department|A part of an organisation with a particular function.|Send the form to the payroll department.
workplace|The place where people do their jobs.|Food must not be prepared in the workplace kitchen after closing.
recruitment|The process of finding and employing staff.|The recruitment process includes a practical test.
applicant|Someone who formally asks for a job or place.|Each applicant must provide two references.
candidate|Someone being considered for a job or position.|The successful candidate will start in April.
application|A formal request for a job, place or service.|Your application must arrive before Friday.
CV|A document describing your education, skills and work history.|Please attach your CV to the application email.
cover letter|A letter explaining why you are suitable for a job.|Use your cover letter to explain your customer-service experience.
reference|A statement about someone's suitability or previous work.|The employer asked my former manager for a reference.
referee|Someone who provides information about your suitability.|Choose a referee who knows your work well.
interview|A meeting to assess someone for a job or place.|Your interview will include a short presentation.
shortlist|A small group of candidates selected for further consideration.|The panel has agreed on a shortlist of five applicants.
qualification|A formal achievement showing knowledge or skills.|The position requires a recognised childcare qualification.
experience|Knowledge or skill gained by doing something.|Previous retail experience would be helpful.
skill|An ability to do a task well.|Clear communication is an essential skill for this role.
position|A job or role within an organisation.|This position involves occasional weekend work.
role|The duties expected of someone in a particular situation.|Your role includes welcoming visitors.
duty|A task that someone is expected to perform.|Checking the alarm is the supervisor's final duty.
responsibility|Something you are expected to deal with or look after.|Stock control will be your main responsibility.
job description|A document explaining the tasks and conditions of a job.|Read the job description before applying.
contract|An agreement setting out duties and conditions.|Keep a signed copy of your employment contract.
permanent|Intended to continue without a fixed end date.|The company is advertising a permanent receptionist position.
temporary|Continuing for a limited period.|We need temporary staff during the summer.
full-time|For the normal complete working week.|The vacancy is a full-time position.
part-time|For fewer hours than a normal working week.|She works part-time while attending college.
flexible|Able to change to suit different needs.|The employer offers flexible working hours.
induction|An introduction to a new job or organisation.|New employees attend induction on their first morning.
orientation|An introduction that helps someone understand a new setting.|The orientation session includes a tour of the building.
training|Activities that develop knowledge or practical skills.|Paid training is provided before you use the equipment.
promotion|A move to a job with greater responsibility or status.|She applied for promotion to team leader.
performance|How well someone carries out their work.|The review considers attendance and overall performance.
target|A result that a person or team aims to achieve.|Our monthly target is to reduce unanswered calls.
deadline|The latest time by which something must be done.|The deadline for submitting expenses is Thursday.
workload|The amount of work someone has to complete.|Please speak up if your workload becomes unmanageable.
schedule|A plan showing when activities will take place.|Check the weekly schedule before arranging appointments.
shift|A period during which someone is scheduled to work.|The evening shift starts at four o'clock.
rota|A list showing who works at which times.|The new rota will be posted on Monday.
overtime|Time worked beyond normal working hours.|Ask for approval before working overtime.
break|A short period of rest during work.|Take your lunch break before the afternoon delivery.
leave|Authorised time away from work.|Apply for leave through the staff website.
annual leave|Paid time off work available each year.|Please book annual leave at least two weeks ahead.
sick leave|Time away from work because of illness.|Notify your supervisor before taking sick leave.
parental leave|Time away from work to care for a new child.|The handbook explains how to request parental leave.
absence|A period when someone is not at work or an expected place.|Please explain your absence on the return-to-work form.
punctuality|The habit of arriving at the expected time.|Punctuality is important because the reception desk must be staffed.
attendance|Being present at work or a scheduled activity.|Attendance at the safety workshop is compulsory.
salary|A fixed amount of pay for a job.|The advertised salary is paid monthly.
wage|Pay for work, often calculated by the hour.|The hourly wage increases after the training period.
payroll|The system used to calculate and pay staff wages.|Give your bank details to the payroll team.
payslip|A document showing pay and deductions.|Check your payslip for the overtime payment.
bonus|Extra money paid in addition to normal pay.|Staff may receive a bonus for meeting the annual target.
allowance|Money provided for a particular expense.|Employees travelling overnight receive a meal allowance.
pension|Money paid regularly after someone retires.|The employer contributes to the staff pension scheme.
benefit|An advantage provided in addition to normal pay.|A discounted travel pass is one employee benefit.
retirement|The point at which someone stops regular paid work.|The team organised a gathering for her retirement.
equality|Equal treatment, rights or opportunities.|The employer promotes equality in access to training.
union|An organisation that represents workers' interests.|The union representative attended the pay discussion.
confidential|Intended to be kept private.|Do not leave confidential staff files on the desk.
professional|Showing the standards expected in a job.|Please use professional language when replying to customers.
reliable|Able to be trusted to do what is expected.|We need a reliable person to open the shop.
cooperation|Working together to achieve a result.|The project depends on cooperation between departments.
leadership|The ability to guide and support other people.|The course develops practical leadership skills.
priority|Something that needs attention before other things.|Customer safety is our first priority.
procedure|An agreed series of steps for doing something.|Follow the procedure for reporting missing stock.
policy|An organisation's official approach or set of rules.|Read the policy on working from home.
handbook|A book or document giving practical rules and information.|The staff handbook explains the holiday system.
meeting|An arranged gathering to discuss something.|The team meeting will start at nine.
agenda|A list of topics to discuss at a meeting.|Please add the delivery problem to the agenda.
minutes|The written record of what happened at a meeting.|The minutes will be emailed to everyone tomorrow.
briefing|A short session giving important instructions or information.|Attend the morning briefing before starting your shift.
report|A document describing facts, findings or events.|Submit a short report after visiting the supplier.
feedback|Comments intended to help someone improve.|Your supervisor will give feedback after the first week.
teamwork|People working together effectively.|The exercise tests teamwork rather than individual speed.
competence|The ability to perform a task to a suitable standard.|The assessment checks competence in handling customer complaints.
probation|An initial period during which a new employee is assessed.|Your progress will be reviewed at the end of probation.
appraisal|A formal discussion of someone's work performance.|Your annual appraisal includes setting new goals.
reimbursement|Repayment of money someone has spent.|Keep your receipts to claim reimbursement for travel.
redundancy|Loss of a job because the role is no longer needed.|The company offered retraining after the redundancy announcement.
dismissal|The ending of someone's employment by the employer.|The handbook explains the procedure for appealing a dismissal.
grievance|A formal complaint about unfair treatment at work.|You can discuss a grievance with the personnel officer.
discrimination|Unfair treatment based on personal characteristics.|The policy prohibits discrimination during recruitment.
harassment|Repeated unwanted behaviour that causes distress.|Report harassment through the confidential staff service.
negotiation|Discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.|The negotiation concerned working hours and pay.
consultation|A process of asking for views before making a decision.|Staff consultation will take place before the rota changes.
initiative|The ability to act without waiting to be told.|The role requires initiative when dealing with unexpected problems.
delegation|Giving another person responsibility for a task.|Effective delegation allows the supervisor to focus on urgent work.
productivity|The amount of useful work produced.|Better equipment has improved productivity in the workshop.
efficiency|Doing work well without wasting time or resources.|The new booking system should improve efficiency.
accountability|The duty to explain and take responsibility for actions.|The new system improves accountability for spending.
workforce|All the people working for an organisation or industry.|The company is expanding its local workforce.
commission|Pay based on the value of sales someone makes.|The sales role includes a basic salary and commission.
resignation|The formal act of leaving a job voluntarily.|Please submit your resignation in writing.
work-life balance|A reasonable division between work and personal life.|Flexible hours can improve work-life balance.
